title: Free abelian sheaf resolution of a site hypercover
statement: Let $\mathcal D$ be a small site with finite limits [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] [def-weil-size-convention], let $W\in\mathcal D$, and let $V_\bullet\to W$ be an augmented simplicial object [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object]. Put $N_0=W$ and, for $p>0$, let $N_p$ be the finite matching limit in $\mathcal D/W$ of the compatible proper faces of a $p$-simplex. Assume the sieve generated by $V_p\to N_p$ is covering for every $p\geq0$: there is a covering $\{N_{p,k}\to N_p\}_k$ of $\mathcal D$ each member of which factors through $V_p\to N_p$. Let $\mathbf Z[V_p]$ denote the sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] of the free abelian presheaf on the representable $V_p$. Then the augmented alternating-face complex of abelian sheaves $\cdots\to\mathbf Z[V_2]\to\mathbf Z[V_1]\to\mathbf Z[V_0]\to\mathbf Z[W]\to0$ is exact (its degree-zero homology is $\mathbf Z[W]$ and its positive homology sheaves vanish).

source.place: Tags 01GE (lemma-acyclic-hypercover-sheaves), 01GC--01GD (free simplicial abelian resolution), and 01GW (lemma-injective-trivial-cech), with the coskeleton comparison in the proof of 01GE.

proof.text: Write $K_q=h_{V_q}$ and $G=h_W$ for the representable presheaves, with the given augmentation $K\to G$. For every $p$ the map $h_{V_p}\to h_{N_p}$ has local lifts of every section: pull back the covering of $N_p$ along a section $U\to N_p$, then use its given factorizations through $V_p$. This also makes its sheafification epic. Indeed, two maps out of $h_{N_p}^{\#}$ agreeing on $h_{V_p}^{\#}$ agree on every section of $h_{N_p}$ by these local lifts and sheaf separatedness, hence agree by the sheafification universal property. The cited epi criterion therefore makes the sheafified map locally surjective. This reasoning does not require the site to be subcanonical.

source.place: Tag 01GE, hypotheses (1)-(3); verification from the covering-sieve hypotheses.

proof.text: Define $K^0_q=K_0\times_G\cdots\times_GK_0$ ($q+1$ factors), with faces deleting and degeneracies repeating factors. This is the relative Cech nerve of $K_0\to G$. Step 1 for $p=0$ verifies the local surjectivity required by the Cech free-homology lemma. With $R=\mathbf Z$ that lemma gives $H_i(K^0)=0$ for $i>0$ and identifies $H_0(K^0)$ with $\mathbf Z[G]^{\#}$ via the augmentation.

source.place: Tags 01GC (lemma-compare-cosk0) and 01GE (lemma-acyclic-hypercover-sheaves), separately defined relative fibre-product base stage.

proof.text: For $n\geq1$ form the ordinary presheaf coskeleta $K^n=\operatorname{cosk}_n\mathrm{sk}_nK$. The finite-limit description gives $K^n_q=K_q$ for $q\leq n$. It also shows that an $m$-coskeleton $A$ is $n$-coskeletal for $n\geq m$: a compatible cone of simplices of $A$ of dimension at most $n$ restricts to its cone in dimensions at most $m$; conversely, the latter cone uniquely supplies every higher entry by the displayed limit formula for $A_q$. These two operations are inverse and commute with all simplicial operators. The coskeleton universal property supplies the maps $K^n\to K^{n-1}$ for $n\geq2$, inducing the identity in degrees below $n$.

source.place: Tag 018B, lemma-cosk-up, clauses (3)-(4); the cone calculation from the finite-limit coskeleton formula.

proof.text: The new relative-nerve lemma says $K^0$ is $1$-coskeletal. The degree-zero augmentation of $K^1$, whose degrees zero and one equal those of $K$, extends to an augmentation $K^1\to G$: all vertices have the same image in $G$ because their connecting edges are in $K_1$ and the two endpoints of each such edge have equal augmentation. Apply the lemma with $T=K^1$ and $g=\mathrm{id}_{K_0}$ to obtain $K^1\to K^0$, with its vertex-tuple formula. In degree zero it is the identity and in degree one it is $(d_1,d_0):K_1\to K_0\times_GK_0=h_{V_0\times_WV_0}$. Here $N_1=V_0\times_WV_0$, so Step 1 gives the needed local surjectivity. Both objects are $1$-coskeletal. Apply the homology-comparison lemma at $n=1$, $R=\mathbf Z$, to get an isomorphism on every homology sheaf.

source.place: Tag 01GE, first transition K^1 to the relative nerve K^0; Tag 018I (simplicial.tex, lemma-cosk-minus-one) supplies its universal property.

proof.text: For $n\geq2$, the ordinary matching object for $K$ agrees with $h_{N_n}$, although $N_n$ was defined in the slice over $W$. To check this, evaluate at $U$: Yoneda sends the finite slice limit to tuples of compatible proper faces with a common map $U\to W$. Any compatible tuple in the ordinary matching limit already has that common map: the boundary of an $n$-simplex contains all its edges, so augmentation equality along edges equates the images of all vertices; every higher face has that same image. Forgetting the common map and recovering it from any vertex are inverse operations. These operations commute with restrictions in $U$ and with the maps from $K_n$. The matching/coskeleton node now identifies $(K^{n-1})_n$ with $h_{N_n}$ and its canonical map from $K_n$ with $h_{V_n}\to h_{N_n}$.

source.place: Tag 01GE, hypothesis (3); explicit comparison with the relative matching limit in this item.

proof.text: For $n\geq2$, apply the comparison lemma to $K^n\to K^{n-1}$, with $R=\mathbf Z$. Step 3 gives the identity below degree $n$ and shows both objects are $n$-coskeletal; Steps 1 and 5 give local surjectivity in degree $n$. Hence every induced homology map is an isomorphism. Together with Step 4 this gives $H_i(K^n)\simeq H_i(K^0)$ for all $n\geq1$. Every comparison respects the augmentations: they are determined by the common image of a vertex in $G$, and all comparison maps preserve those vertices.

source.place: Tags 01GD (lemma-acyclicity) and 01GE, induction for n at least 2 after the separate n=1 transition.

proof.text: Fix $i\geq0$ and choose $n\geq i+1$. The counit identification in degrees at most $n$ identifies the alternating-face complexes of $K$ and $K^n$ in degrees $i-1,i,i+1$ (only degrees zero and one are needed if $i=0$), together with their differentials. Thus their degree-$i$ homology sheaves agree. Steps 2, 4 and 6 give vanishing for $i>0$ and $H_0(K)=\mathbf Z[G]^{\#}$. The degree-zero isomorphism is the original augmentation because each comparison commutes with augmentation. Consequently it is surjective and has kernel the image of the degree-one boundary, which proves the whole displayed augmented exact sequence.

source.place: Tag 01GE, conclusion by fixed-degree stabilization and augmentation compatibility.
